question: When two statements or comparisons are apparently contradictory, we have an example of
solution:
A paradox is a statement or comparison that seems contradictory but may still be true.

Irony is a contrast between what is expected and what happens; contrast is a general difference; parallelism is balanced grammatical structure.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The theme of a literary work is the

option.a: different views on a particular topic
option.d: interesting issues raised in the work

solution:
A theme is the central idea or the dominant concern that runs through a literary work.

It is more than a topic or an interesting issue; it is the main idea the writer keeps exploring.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: When a protagonist is purged of the dominant emotions of pity and fear at the end of a tragedy, it is called
solution:
Catharsis is the emotional cleansing or purging of pity and fear that the audience experiences at the end of a tragedy.

Redemption means rescue or salvation, while dementia is unrelated to drama.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: An exaggeration or overstatement in literature is a
solution:
Hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration or overstatement used for emphasis or effect.

A metaphor is a comparison, a soliloquy is a speech made alone on stage, and a hexameter is a metrical line.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: A melodramatic play is based on
solution:
Melodrama relies on sensational plots, exaggerated characters, and strong emotional appeal.

It is not defined by didactic overtones, pleasant music, or events that calm down.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: In drama, a conspicuous weakness in the character of the protagonist contributing to his downfall is referred to as
solution:
A tragic flaw (hamartia) is a weakness in the protagonist that helps to bring about his downfall.

Catharsis is emotional purging, anagnorisis is a moment of recognition, and catastrophe is the final disaster.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: Comic relief is

option.a: a device used in the theatre where a play ends in marriage
option.b: the use of hearty and wholesome laughter in plays
option.c: a figure of speech used in comic theatre
option.d: the use of humorous characters' speeches or scenes in a tragic work

solution:
Comic relief is a humorous scene, speech, or character introduced into a serious or tragic work.

It breaks tension for the audience; it is not simply a play ending in marriage or a figure of speech.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The technique used to bring the plot of a play to an abrupt end is called
solution:
Deus ex machina is an unexpected intervention or device that solves a difficult situation and ends the plot abruptly.

Denouement is the gradual unravelling of the plot, while “endnote” and “startnote” are not dramatic techniques.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: When a story is told in a song and passed down by word of mouth, it is called
solution:
A ballad is a song-like narrative poem that is often passed down orally.

A sonnet is a fourteen-line poem, an epic is a long heroic narrative, and “a singer's story” is not the literary term.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The poem above is memorable for its
section:
Ibadan, running splash of rust and gold – flung and scattered among seven hills like broken china in the sun.
— J.P. Clark, “Ibadan”
solution:
The extract uses vivid, musical language and striking imagery: “running splash of rust and gold” and “broken china in the sun”.

This song-like, emotional quality is lyricism. A simile is present (“like broken china”), but the question asks what makes the whole poem memorable.

Pun and heroism are not the main qualities here, so option B is correct.

question: The landscape described in the passage above is
section:
Going up the river was like travelling back to the earliest beginnings of the world when vegetation rioted on the earth, and the big trees were kings. An empty stream, a great silence, an impenetrable forest. The air was warm, thick, heavy, sluggish.

— Joseph Conrad, Heart of Darkness
solution:
The landscape is huge, dark, silent, and threatening: “impenetrable forest” and air that is “warm, thick, heavy, sluggish”.

This creates an atmosphere that is awe-inspiring and fearful, that is, formidable.

It is certainly not friendly; “hostile” is close but too one-sided, while option C best captures both awe and fear.

question: The beauty of this poem is built upon its

option.a: extended images of treasure and gun

section:
“…Akosua Nowa has touched my manhood;
Tell her, red ant upon the tree;
If she passes this way, I am gone,
I am gone to load my gun
No matter how hidden deep her treasure,
By my father's coffin I swear
I'll shoot my way to it this day;
Son of the hunter King
There is liquid fire in my gun!”
— Joe de Graft, “Akosua Nowa”
solution:
The poem sustains images of the treasure, the gun, the red ant, and “liquid fire” across several lines.

These recurring, extended images build the poem's beauty and intensity.

Boastfulness is the persona's tone, not the source of the poem's beauty; line arrangement and rhythm are secondary, so option A is correct.

question: The above lines are an example of
section:
“With beaded bubbles winking at the brim,
And purple-stained mouth,”
— John Keats, “Ode to a Nightingale”
solution:
“beaded bubbles” repeats the initial /b/ sound, and “purple-stained” adds a /p/ sound.

The repetition of initial consonant sounds is alliteration.

Tautology is needless repetition of meaning, euphemism is mild language, and comic relief is a dramatic device, so option A is correct.

question: One dominant image presented in the poem above is that of
section:
The leaves are withered. Roses fold and shrink
Dog, the panting athlete shows his tongue
A dwarfed shadow flees. Hides under legs.
Nuts wrinkle and crack
— W. Kamera, “Poems in Four Parts”
solution:
Withered leaves, shrinking roses, a panting dog, a fleeing shadow, and cracked nuts all suggest intense heat and drought.

Together these are images of summer.

Tiredness and spent life are possible feelings, but the dominant seasonal image is summer; death is too extreme, so option D is correct.

question: In the passage above, the author evokes the atmosphere of
section:
“At the most remote end of the crypt there appeared another less spacious. Its walls had been lined with human remains piled to the vault overhead, in the fashion of the great catacombs of Paris. Three sides of this interior crypt were still ornamented in this manner. From the fourth the bones had been thrown down, and lay promiscuously upon the earth, forming at one point a mound of some size.”

— Edgar Allan Poe, “The Cask of Amontillado”
solution:
The crypt, human remains, scattered bones, and darkness create a gloomy, fatal atmosphere.

This is an atmosphere of doom — the feeling that death and disaster are near.

Cannibalism and monstrosity are not suggested, and “evil” is too abstract, so option C is correct.

question: The dominant device in the extract above is
section: “Beautiful Kareendi, flower of my heart. No one but you can type them. For I want to send them care of the address of your heart, by the post of your heart, to be read by the eye of your heart, thereafter to be kept within your heart, sealed there forever and ever.”
solution:
The phrase “of your heart” is repeated and expanded: the address of your heart, the post of your heart, the eye of your heart, kept within your heart.

This repetition builds in intensity and detail, which is progressive amplification.

It is more than simple repetition or contrast, so option C is correct.

question: Effect in the above passage is achieved through the use of
section:
“A slight breeze murmured in the air. Grasses swayed as if in resentment. Over the horizon, just beneath the spectrum of the ascending sun, horizontal bands of red cloud hung menacingly above the tips of the trees and the morning air smelled of burnt clay.”

— Isidore Okpewho, The Victims
solution:
The passage appeals strongly to sight: red cloud, the ascending sun, swaying grasses, and burnt clay.

The effect is therefore achieved mainly through visual images.

Detailed description and punctuation support the effect, but the dominant device is visual imagery; the tone is not subdued, so option A is correct.

question: The writer of the lines above

option.a: is critical of the modern woman
option.c: shuns the old type of woman

section:
Ocol rejects the old type.
He is in love with a modern woman
He is in love with a beautiful girl
Who speaks English.
— Okot p'Bitek, “Song of Lawino”
solution:
The lines present Ocol rejecting the “old type” and choosing a girl simply because she “speaks English”.

The writer is mocking Ocol's shallow value judgment.

The poem does not attack the modern woman or praise English speakers, so option B is correct.

question: The mood in the lines above is one of
section:
“You amble on
we can no longer wait for nature's course
we must deliver you with force”
— Amelia House, “Our Sun Rises”
solution:
“We can no longer wait” and “we must deliver you with force” express impatience and anger.

The mood is therefore indignation.

It is not joy, fear, or sorrow, so option C is correct.

question: In the stanza above, the poet recognizes that
section:
“SINCE I am coming to that Holy roome,
Where, with thy Quire of Saints for evermore
I shall be made thy Musique; As I come
I tune the Instrument here at the dore,
And what I must doe then, thinke here before.”
— John Donne, “Hymn to God my God”
solution:
The poet speaks of “coming to that Holy roome” and tuning the instrument “here at the dore”.

These images suggest that he is preparing for death and the afterlife, so he recognizes that he is near his death.

He is not literally a choir master; the other options miss the central meaning, so option A is correct.

question: What theme is emphasised when bride prices are accepted from multiple chiefs?
section: This question is based on The Marriage of Anansewa.
solution:
Ananse accepts bride prices and gifts from several chiefs for one daughter.

This treats Anansewa as a valuable object to be traded for wealth, which is the commodification of women.

The play is not about national unity, colonial resistance, or heroism in this scene, so option C is correct.

question: Which of these best describes Ananse?
section: This question is based on The Marriage of Anansewa.
solution:
Ananse lies to four chiefs, collects their gifts, and stages Anansewa's death to escape the consequences.

These are the actions of a trickster.

He is poor, but “wise but poor” misses his cunning; he is neither generous nor naive, so option C is correct.

question: Antony blames Cleopatra for

option.b: causing the loss at Actium by fleeing

section: This question is based on Antony and Cleopatra.
solution:
After the sea battle at Actium, Cleopatra's ships flee and Antony follows them.

Antony later accuses Cleopatra of fleeing and causing his defeat.

He does not blame her for marrying Caesar, betraying him to Octavius, or urging war with Lepidus, so option B is correct.

question: What emotion drives Enobarbus in this speech?
section:
This question is based on Antony and Cleopatra.

Enobarbus: “I am alone the villain of the earth,
And feel I am so most. O Antony,
Thou mine of bounty, how wouldst thou have paid
My better service, when my turpitude
Thou dost so crown with gold!”
solution:
Enobarbus has deserted Antony, yet Antony sends his treasure after him.

Enobarbus calls himself “the villain of the earth” and feels unworthy of Antony's generosity.

This is guilt, not revenge, gratitude, or pride, so option D is correct.

question: Fina's character is best described as
section: This question is based on So the Path Does Not Die.
solution:
Fina survives circumcision, rape, displacement, and the challenges of life in America, and she keeps rebuilding her life.

This shows resilience — the ability to recover and keep going.

She is not passive, irrational, or detached, so option C is correct.
category: So the Path Does Not Die

question: Fina's insistence on supporting her sister Isa, despite Cammy's protest, stems from
section: This question is based on So the Path Does Not Die.
solution:
Fina keeps supporting Isa because she believes in family obligation and does not want to “cut the rope”.

This reflects African communal values, where the individual remains tied to the family and community.

It is not mainly religious guilt, feminism, or political ideology, so option D is correct.
category: So the Path Does Not Die

question: What is the significance of Cobra's polite and religious demeanor after the war?

option.a: It disguises unresolved guilt and denial
option.b: It shows he has been reformed

section: This question is based on Redemption Road.
solution:
After the war, Cobra presents himself as a polite, religious man, but he is still involved in corruption and violence.

His respectable image disguises unresolved guilt and denial about his wartime crimes.

He is not reformed, innocent, or preparing for exile, so option A is correct.

question: Letter-writing in the novel serves as
section: This question is based on Redemption Road.
solution:
Bendu writes a symbolic letter to those who hurt her, and Tenneh writes to her mother.

Writing helps them confront trauma and begin to heal, so it is a tool for personal healing.

It is not propaganda, legal testimony, or political indoctrination, so option B is correct.

question: Which narrative technique best defines the structure of the novel?
section: This question is based on Path of Lucas: The Journey He Endured.
solution:
The novel frames Lucas's life story as a present-day hospital vigil, then moves back into the past and across several decades.

This is a non-linear flashback structure.

It is not stream of consciousness, a novel in letters, or a detached third-person omniscient narration, so option A is correct.
category: Path of Lucas: The Journey He Endured

question: What does Lucas's refusal to remarry after Isabelle's death reveal about his core values?

option.c: His loyalty and emotional fidelity transcend death
option.d: He feels guilty for her illness

section: This question is based on Path of Lucas: The Journey He Endured.
solution:
After Isabelle dies, Lucas does not remarry and continues to honour her memory.

This shows loyalty and emotional fidelity that transcend death.

He does not hate women, act from social pressure, or merely feel guilty, so option C is correct.
category: Path of Lucas: The Journey He Endured

question: The line “like a fixed portrait smile” suggests that the speaker's smile is
section: This question is based on Once Upon a Time.
solution:
“Like a fixed portrait smile” compares the smile to a painted portrait that cannot change.

This suggests a fake, artificial smile, not a genuine one.

It is not artistic in a positive sense or constantly changing, so option B is correct.

question: What is the thematic preoccupation of this poem?

option.a: The past should never be erased

section: This question is based on New Tongue.
solution:
The poem laments the younger generation's abandonment of their language and traditions.

Its message is that the past and cultural roots should never be erased.

It does not say the past should be rewritten or that memory is irrelevant, so option A is correct.

question: “Faceless, silent as night thieves” contributes to which theme in the poem?
section: This question is based on Night.
solution:
“Faceless, silent as night thieves” presents the night as stealthy and threatening.

This creates a sense of dread and contributes to the theme of fear.

It does not suggest freedom, truth, or celebration, so option C is correct.

question: A central theme in the poem is
section: This question is based on Not My Business.
solution:
The persona ignores the arrests of his neighbours because they do not affect him.

This is political complacency — the failure to act against injustice until it reaches one's own door.

It is not greed, courage, or success, so option B is correct.

question: What is the occasion that inspires the poem?
section: This question is based on Hearty Garlands.
solution:
The poem honours an elder who has reached eighty-five and celebrates his achievements and wisdom.

The occasion is therefore an eighty-fifth birthday celebration.

It is not a retirement, funeral, or political victory, so option B is correct.

question: The image “coelacanth was recaptured” suggests

option.d: the rediscovery of something ancient and resilient

section: This question is based on The Breast of the Sea.
solution:
The coelacanth is an ancient fish once thought extinct but later found alive.

The image therefore suggests the rediscovery of something ancient and resilient.

It is not about domination, a military operation, or a myth, so option D is correct.

question: What does the poet mean by “all that's best of dark and bright”?

option.a: The woman is both good and evil
option.d: She reflects a perfect balance of opposites

section: This question is based on She Walks in Beauty.
solution:
The phrase refers to the woman's dark hair and bright features coming together in harmony.

It means she reflects a perfect balance of opposites, not that she is morally good and evil.

The line does not suggest confusion or indecision, so option D is correct.

question: The final escape of Chanticleer is due to
section: This question is based on The Nun's Priest's Tale.
solution:
Chanticleer escapes by flattering the fox, persuading him to open his mouth to boast.

The fox loosens his grip, and Chanticleer flies away. The escape is due to his use of flattery.

It is not his flying ability alone, the hen's distraction, or the widow's intervention, so option B is correct.

question: The term “Ultra-Super Global Special” is an example of
section: This question is based on The Telephone Call.
solution:
“Ultra-Super Global Special” is an exaggerated, inflated name for the fake prize.

Deliberate exaggeration is hyperbole.

Litotes is understatement, synecdoche uses a part for a whole, and paradox is a seeming contradiction, so option A is correct.

question: The woman's final sigh symbolises

option.a: the release of her lover's spirit
option.d: the end of the carving process

section: This question is based on The Stone.
solution:
After the stone is finished, the woman breathes her lover's name and sighs.

The sigh releases the grief she had held in silently, so it symbolises the release of pent-up sorrow.

It does not release his spirit, show readiness to remarry, or merely mark the end of carving, so option B is correct.

question: The substitution of the name of a part of something for the whole thing is called
solution:
Synecdoche is a figure of speech in which a part stands for the whole, or the whole stands for a part, as in “all hands on deck” where hands means workers.

Metonymy replaces a thing with something closely associated with it (for example, “the crown” for the king). A simile compares two things using like or as, while irony is a contrast between expectation and reality.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The highest point of tension in a story, where the conflict is most intense, is called the
solution:
The climax is the turning point of a story. It is the moment when the conflict reaches its greatest intensity and the outcome begins to be decided.

The exposition introduces the characters and background, the resolution settles the conflict at the end, and suspense is the feeling of uncertainty about what will happen next.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: A speech delivered by a character who is alone on stage and reveals his private thoughts is a
solution:
A soliloquy is a speech made by a character who is alone on stage. It lets the audience hear the character's innermost thoughts and feelings.

An aside is a short remark made to the audience in the presence of other characters. A chorus is a group that comments on the action, and a dialogue is a conversation between two or more characters.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: A literary work that uses humour to expose and correct the vices of society is called
solution:
Satire uses humour, ridicule or irony to expose the foolishness and vices of individuals or society, with the aim of correcting them.

A tragedy ends in disaster, an elegy is a poem that mourns the dead, and a romance is a story of love and adventure.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The use of “the crown” to refer to the monarch is an example of
solution:
Metonymy is the use of the name of something closely associated with a person or thing in place of that person or thing. “The crown” is associated with royalty, so it is used to mean the monarch.

Synecdoche would be a part standing for the whole (for example, “a fleet of fifty sails” for fifty ships). Hyperbole is exaggeration, and an oxymoron joins two opposite words.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: A group of four lines in a poem is called a
solution:
A quatrain is a stanza of four lines. It is one of the commonest stanza forms in English poetry.

A couplet has two lines, a tercet has three lines, and a sestet has six lines.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The repetition of vowel sounds in neighbouring words is known as
solution:
Assonance is the repetition of vowel sounds in nearby words, as in “the eagle easily eats”.

Alliteration repeats initial consonant sounds, consonance repeats consonant sounds within words, and onomatopoeia uses words that imitate sounds, such as “buzz”.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: A story in which characters and events represent abstract ideas is called
solution:
An allegory is a story in which the characters, setting and events stand for abstract ideas or moral qualities. For example, a character named “Greed” may stand for the love of money.

A fable is a short story, often with animal characters, that teaches a moral. A legend is a traditional story about a real person or event, and a myth explains beliefs or natural events.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: A play that ends in disaster, usually with the death of the hero, is a
solution:
A tragedy is a serious play in which the main character suffers greatly and usually dies at the end. The hero's downfall often comes from a weakness in his character or from fate.

A comedy ends happily, a farce is an exaggerated and humorous play, and a melodrama uses sensational events and exaggerated emotions.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The feeling or atmosphere that a literary work creates in the reader is its
solution:
Mood is the emotional atmosphere that a literary work creates in the reader. It may be sad, tense, joyful, frightening or peaceful.

The theme is the central idea or message, the plot is the arrangement of events, and diction is the writer's choice of words.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The lines above suggest that time

option.c: passes and leaves only fading memory

section:
“The tireless river flows
Beneath the bridge of our years;
It bears our names away
And gives them back as echoes.”
solution:
The river is a metaphor for time. It carries our names away and returns them only as echoes, which are faint and fading. This shows that time passes and leaves behind only a weak memory of us.

Option A is too absolute, since echoes still remain. Option B is the opposite of the poem's message, and option D contradicts the image of a flowing river.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The dominant figure of speech in the lines about the moon and the night is
section:
“The moon is a golden coin
Tossed into the night's dark purse.”
solution:
The moon is directly described as a golden coin and the night as a dark purse. These are metaphors because the comparison is stated directly without like or as.

A simile would say the moon is like a golden coin. Personification gives human qualities to non-human things, and hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The dominant figure of speech in the passage above is
section: The market was a sea of heads, and the traders' voices rose and fell above it.
solution:
The market is directly called a sea of heads. This is a metaphor: the crowd is compared to a sea because it is large and moving, but the comparison is stated directly.

A simile would use like or as. A euphemism uses a mild expression for something unpleasant, and an apostrophe addresses someone absent or a non-human thing.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The mood of the exchange between Otto and Martha is one of
section:
OTTO: Why do you tremble whenever the gate is opened?
MARTHA: Every knock is my husband's fist returning.
solution:
Martha trembles and expects every knock to be her husband's fist. This creates an atmosphere of fear and apprehension.

There is no joy, calmness or open anger in her words; she is frightened and waiting for something bad to happen.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The theme of the lines about flags and rivers is
section:
“They have planted their flags upon our hills
And named our rivers in a tongue not ours.”
solution:
Planting flags on another people's hills and renaming their rivers in a foreign language are acts of conquest. The lines therefore speak of colonial domination and the loss of culture.

The lines do not celebrate the beauty of rivers, the joy of travel or friendship; they describe taking control of a people's land and identity.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The figure of speech used in the description of the poor soul is
section:
“Poor soul, she wore her poverty like a royal robe,
And smiled as though the world owed her nothing.”
solution:
The word like makes a direct comparison between her poverty and a royal robe. This is a simile.

A metaphor would say her poverty was a royal robe. An oxymoron joins opposite words, and litotes is an understatement made by denying the opposite.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The device used in the extract above is
section:
“The honourable member rose to speak of honesty,
Then counted the banknotes beneath his desk.”
solution:
The member speaks about honesty while secretly counting bribe money. This contrast between what is said and what is done is irony.

Hyperbole is exaggeration, onomatopoeia uses sound-imitating words, and euphemism replaces harsh words with mild ones. None of these is the main device here.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The figure of speech used in the description of the roof is
section: The rain came down in sheets, and the roof, tired of holding up the sky, finally gave way.
solution:
The roof is said to be tired and to have given way after holding up the sky. These are human qualities given to an inanimate object, so the device is personification.

Metonymy substitutes an associated name, antithesis balances opposite ideas, and a pun plays on the meanings of a word.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: Aloho travels to Jabu in search of
section: This question is based on Harvest of Corruption.
solution:
Aloho leaves her home and goes to Jabu hoping to find a job. Her need for work is what makes her easy prey for Ochuole, who promises her employment.

She is not looking for a husband, her mother or education. Her search for employment is the trap that leads to her downfall.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: Chief Haladu Ade-Amaka is the Minister of
section: This question is based on Harvest of Corruption.
solution:
Chief Haladu Ade-Amaka is the Minister of External Relations. He uses the ministry and its foreign trips to run a drug-trafficking business.

His position is important because it gives him the power and protection that make his corruption possible.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The character who persistently advises Aloho against Ochuole is
section: This question is based on Harvest of Corruption.
solution:
Ogeyi Ogar is Aloho's true friend. She warns Aloho repeatedly to avoid Ochuole and to run away from temptation, but Aloho refuses to listen.

Madam Hoha is part of the corrupt ring, ACP Yakubu is the honest policeman, and Mrs Obi is the Chief's secretary.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: Iago resents Othello chiefly because Othello
section: This question is based on Othello.
solution:
Iago is angry that Othello passed him over and chose Cassio as his lieutenant. He also suspects that Othello has slept with his wife, Emilia.

These grievances feed his hatred and drive his plan to destroy Othello, Desdemona and Cassio.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: Othello kills Desdemona because he believes that she
section: This question is based on Othello.
solution:
Iago convinces Othello that Desdemona is having an affair with Cassio. Othello's jealousy grows until he smothers her in bed.

Desdemona is innocent. After her death, Emilia reveals Iago's plot, and Othello realises his terrible mistake.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The handkerchief Othello gives Desdemona is important because Iago uses it to

option.c: identify the thief who stole it

section: This question is based on Othello.
solution:
Iago arranges for the handkerchief to be found in Cassio's possession. He then tells Othello that Desdemona gave it to Cassio as a love token.

The handkerchief therefore becomes the “proof” that convinces Othello of Desdemona's infidelity, even though she is innocent.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The novel is set mainly in
section: This question is based on Faceless.
solution:
Faceless is set mainly in Accra, Ghana. Its events move between the city's poor streets, the market area of Agbogbloshie and the homes of the middle class.

The setting is important because it shows how poverty and neglect push children like Fofo and Baby T onto the streets.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: Kabria works for an organisation known as
section: This question is based on Faceless.
solution:
Kabria works with MUTE, a non-governmental organisation that campaigns for women's rights and helps poor women and children.

Her work with MUTE gives her the courage and resources to investigate the death of Baby T and to help Fofo.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The title Faceless emphasises the plight of

option.c: poor women and children ignored by society

section: This question is based on Faceless.
solution:
The poor women and children in the novel are faceless in the sense that society does not see them or care about them. People like Maa Tsuru, Fofo and Baby T suffer without help.

The title therefore points to the invisibility and neglect of the poor, not to soldiers, politicians or fishermen.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: Bigger Thomas kills Mary Dalton by
section: This question is based on Native Son.
solution:
Bigger accidentally kills Mary when he smothers her with a pillow to stop her from making noise and getting him into trouble.

He later burns her body in the furnace. This killing is the event that sets the rest of the tragedy in motion.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The lawyer who defends Bigger at his trial is
section: This question is based on Native Son.
solution:
Max is the lawyer who defends Bigger. He argues that Bigger's crimes are the product of a racist society that has denied him dignity and opportunity.

Buckley is the prosecuting attorney, Dalton is Mary's father, and Jan is Mary's boyfriend.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The three sections of the novel are titled
section: This question is based on Native Son.
solution:
Native Son is divided into Fear, Flight and Fate. These titles trace Bigger's movement from a life of fear, through his flight from the police, to his final arrest, trial and sentence.

The other options do not match the actual section titles of the novel.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: Birago Diop suggests that his people suffer because they

option.c: refuse to listen to the wisdom of their ancestors

section: This question is based on Vanity.
solution:
In Vanity, the persona says that the people are deaf to the cries and warnings of their ancestors. They have ignored the wisdom of their forefathers, and so their lives have become empty and futile.

The poem is not about money, farming or markets, but about the loss of ancestral guidance.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The land is compared to a giant whale mainly to show that it

option.d: swallows the hopes and efforts of its people

section: This question is based on Ambush.
solution:
The whale in the poem swallows the sinker, hook, line and bait, so that the fisher's dreams of a good catch are aborted. In the same way, the land destroys the hopes and efforts of its people.

The image is one of greed and destruction, not of plenty or friendliness.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: In Okara's poem, the drums represent
section: This question is based on Piano and Drums.
solution:
The drums speak of primal youth, the jungle and the beginning of things. They represent the persona's African past and tradition.

The piano, on the other hand, speaks of “complex ways” and represents Western civilisation and modernity.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The “dinner” in Hallowell's poem is a metaphor for
section: This question is based on The Dining Table.
solution:
The poem opens with “Dinner tonight comes with gun wounds”. The meal is blood, pain and death, so the dinner stands for war and its destruction.

The imagery of guerrillas, switchblades, cholera and gun wounds confirms that the poem is about war, not a family or religious gathering.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: At thirty, the persona's mood is dominated by
section: This question is based on The Panic of Growing Older.
solution:
At thirty, the persona feels “a sudden throb of pain” and the sense that laboratory tests “have nothing to show”. He is troubled by unfulfilled dreams and the pressure of adulthood.

His earlier hope of “gigantic success” at twenty has given way to disappointment and anxiety.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The anvil and the hammer symbolise

option.d: the shaping of African culture by outside forces

section: This question is based on The Anvil and the Hammer.
solution:
The persona is caught “between the anvil and the hammer” in the forging house of a new life. The two tools stand for the forces of African tradition and Western influence that shape the African.

The poem does not call for the abandonment of African culture. It calls for a careful blend of the old and the new.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: In Tennyson's poem, the “Pilot” is a symbol of
section: This question is based on Crossing the Bar.
solution:
The persona hopes to “see my Pilot face to face” after crossing the bar. The Pilot is God, who guides the soul through death into eternity.

The whole poem is an extended metaphor in which death is a voyage and the bar is the boundary between life and death.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: In Herbert's poem, God withholds from man the gift of
section: This question is based on The Pulley.
solution:
God pours all blessings on man but keeps back rest. Because man is rich and weary, his restlessness will turn him back to God.

The poem uses the image of a pulley to show how God draws man to Himself. The withheld gift is rest, not wealth, sight or wisdom.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: Blake's poem criticises

option.c: formal education that confines the child from nature

section: This question is based on The School Boy.
solution:
The school boy loves the summer morning and the songs of birds, but school keeps him indoors under “a cruel eye outworn”. The poem criticises an education that cages the child and separates him from nature.

Blake is not attacking parents directly, nor is he praising laziness or summer. He is questioning a joyless system of schooling.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: King Jovinian is humiliated in Morris's poem because of his
section: This question is based on The Proud King.
solution:
Jovinian is so proud that he boasts, “Am I not God, while I live at least?” He is then stripped of his royal clothes and identity and treated as a madman.

His pride and arrogance bring about his humiliation, and he learns humility in his old age.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: A short story, usually with animal characters, that teaches a moral lesson is called a
solution:
A fable is a short story, often with animals as characters, that ends with a clear moral lesson. Examples include the stories of the tortoise and the hare.

A parable is also a story with a moral, but its characters are usually human. A folktale is a traditional story passed down orally, and a novella is a short novel.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The narrator who knows the thoughts and feelings of all the characters is called
solution:
An omniscient narrator is “all-knowing”. The narrator can enter the minds of every character and report their private thoughts and feelings.

A first-person narrator uses “I” and knows only what he or she experiences. A limited narrator knows the thoughts of only one character, and an unreliable narrator cannot be fully trusted.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: A group of lines forming a unit in a poem is called a
solution:
A stanza is a group of lines arranged together as a unit in a poem, much like a paragraph in prose.

A canto is a major division of a long poem, a refrain is a repeated line or group of lines, and a couplet is specifically two rhyming lines.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The use of a mild or indirect expression in place of a harsh one is called
solution:
Euphemism replaces a harsh or unpleasant expression with a milder one, such as saying “he passed away” instead of “he died”.

Hyperbole is exaggeration, innuendo is a suggestive remark, and apostrophe is a direct address to someone absent or to a non-human thing.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: A play on the different meanings of a word for humorous effect is called a
solution:
A pun is a play on words that uses two or more meanings of the same word, or words that sound alike, to create humour.

A malapropism is the humorous misuse of a word, a paradox is a seeming contradiction, and an epigram is a short witty saying.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The chief character in a literary work is called the
solution:
The protagonist is the main character, whose actions and fate hold the story together.

The antagonist opposes the protagonist, the narrator tells the story, and a foil is a character whose qualities contrast with another character's.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: A fourteen-line poem written in iambic pentameter is called a
solution:
A sonnet is a poem of fourteen lines, usually written in iambic pentameter and with a fixed rhyme scheme.

A ballad tells a story in short stanzas, an ode is a long lyric poem of praise, and an elegy mourns the dead.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The contrast between what is said and what is actually meant is called
solution:
Verbal irony occurs when a speaker says one thing but means the opposite, as when someone looks at a terrible mess and says, “What a tidy room!”

A paradox is a statement that seems contradictory but may be true. Hyperbole is exaggeration, and metonymy substitutes an associated name.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: A writer's attitude towards his subject matter is known as
solution:
Tone is the writer's attitude towards the subject, the characters or the reader. It may be serious, mocking, sympathetic, angry or humorous.

Mood is the feeling created in the reader, theme is the central idea, and style is the way the writer uses language.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: A long narrative poem celebrating the deeds of a hero is called an
solution:
An epic is a long narrative poem about the great deeds of a hero, often involving battles, journeys and supernatural forces. Examples are Homer's Iliad and Odyssey.

An ode is a lyric poem of praise, an idyll is a short poem about country life, and an epigram is a brief witty saying.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The figure of speech used in the description of the water is
section:
“She carried me on her back
Across the flooded road,
And the water, ashamed,
Parted at her feet.”
solution:
The water is described as being ashamed and as parting at her feet. These are human feelings and actions given to water, so the device is personification.

A simile would use like or as, metonymy substitutes an associated name, and litotes is an understatement.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The mood created by the description of the city is one of
section:
“The city wears a coat of smoke
And coughs through its iron throat.”
solution:
The images of smoke, coughing and an “iron throat” suggest a dirty, unhealthy and unhappy city. The mood is therefore one of gloom and despair.

There is no joy, romance or humour in these lines; the city is presented as sick and choked.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The passage above reveals the character's
section: He counted the coins twice, then a third time, as if arithmetic could multiply them.
solution:
The character counts his few coins again and again, hoping that counting will somehow increase them. This shows poverty and desperation.

Wealthy or generous people would not need to count a small sum three times. Nothing in the passage suggests carelessness.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: Ada's tone in the extract above is
section:
LUKE: The door is open.
ADA: So is my mouth. Say what you came to say.
solution:
Ada's reply is short and sharp. She tells Luke to say what he came to say and refuses to be controlled, showing that she is impatient and defiant.

She is not gentle, timid or sorrowful; her words are bold and dismissive.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The lines above suggest that suffering is caused by

option.c: those who hold power over others

section:
“Do not ask the drum why it weeps;
Ask the hand that beats it.”
solution:
The drum weeps because a hand is beating it. The image means that we should not blame the sufferer but those who use their power to cause suffering.

The lines do not blame the victims, the weather or visitors. The “hand” stands for oppressive power.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The figure of speech used in the description of the compound is
section: The compound was silent; even the goats stood still, as though the earth were holding its breath.
solution:
The earth is said to be holding its breath, which is a human action given to a non-human thing. This is personification.

The phrase “as though” introduces an imaginative comparison, but it is not a straightforward simile using like or as. It is not hyperbole or euphemism either.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The figure of speech used in the description of the sun is
section: The sun was a tired labourer dragging himself to bed behind the hills.
solution:
The sun is directly described as a tired labourer. This is a metaphor because the comparison is stated without like or as.

A simile would say the sun was like a tired labourer. Onomatopoeia imitates sound, and antithesis balances opposite ideas.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The device illustrated in the chairman's remark is
section: “We are all equal,” said the chairman, adjusting the gold chain on his neck.
solution:
The chairman claims that everyone is equal while wearing a gold chain that shows his wealth and superiority. The contrast between his words and his appearance is irony.

There is no exaggeration, sound repetition or direct address to an absent person in the extract.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: Ochuole introduces Aloho to Chief Ade-Amaka as a
section: This question is based on Harvest of Corruption.
solution:
Ochuole presents Aloho to the Chief as a protocol officer. The job is a disguise: the Chief really wants her to carry drugs and to become his mistress.

This false job offer is the bait that traps Aloho.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: Aloho's death is finally caused by
section: This question is based on Harvest of Corruption.
solution:
Aloho becomes pregnant for the Chief and goes from hospital to hospital seeking an abortion. She eventually dies from complications of the abortion.

Her death exposes the heartlessness of the Chief, Ochuole and the corrupt doctor who puts money before life.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The judge who first discharges Chief Ade-Amaka is
section: This question is based on Harvest of Corruption.
solution:
Justice Odili is the corrupt judge who takes bribes from the Chief. He dismisses the drug case against the Chief for “want of evidence”.

His action shows how corruption reaches even the judiciary, which is supposed to protect justice.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: Iago manipulates Roderigo by promising him
section: This question is based on Othello.
solution:
Roderigo is in love with Desdemona. Iago takes money from him and promises that he will help him win Desdemona's love, although Iago knows this is impossible.

Roderigo is therefore used as a tool in Iago's plan to destroy Othello.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: Before the Duke, Brabantio accuses Othello of

option.c: using charms or witchcraft on Desdemona

section: This question is based on Othello.
solution:
Brabantio cannot believe that his daughter would choose Othello freely. He therefore claims that Othello has used charms or witchcraft to win her.

Othello defends himself by telling the story of their courtship, and Desdemona confirms that she loves him willingly.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: Cassio loses his position as lieutenant after
section: This question is based on Othello.
solution:
Iago gets Cassio drunk and provokes him into a fight with Roderigo and Montano. Othello arrives, sees the disorder and dismisses Cassio from his post.

This drunken brawl is part of Iago's plan, because it leaves Cassio desperate and open to Iago's advice.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: Maa Tsuru's daughter who becomes a street child and is later killed is
section: This question is based on Faceless.
solution:
Baby T is Maa Tsuru's daughter. She runs away from home, lives on the streets and is later murdered.

Her death is the crime at the centre of the novel. Fofo is her sister, while Odarley and Vickie are other characters in the story.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The novel chiefly condemns a society that allows

option.b: children to be exploited and abandoned

section: This question is based on Faceless.
solution:
Faceless shows children who are abused, trafficked, forced into prostitution and left to die on the streets. The novel condemns a society that exploits and abandons its children.

Education for women and family life are not the targets of the novel's criticism.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: Kabria's investigation is driven mainly by her
section: This question is based on Faceless.
solution:
Kabria is moved by the suffering of Fofo and the death of Baby T. She risks her time and safety because of her compassion for abused children.

She is not seeking fame or a prize, and she is not acting out of fear of the police.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: Bigger kills Bessie mainly because

option.a: she betrayed him to the police
option.d: he fears she will expose him

section: This question is based on Native Son.
solution:
Bessie knows about Mary's disappearance, and Bigger is afraid that she will talk. He kills her to prevent her from exposing him.

His action shows how fear and desperation drive him to further violence.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The third section of the novel, “Fate”, deals mainly with
section: This question is based on Native Son.
solution:
“Fate” covers Bigger's arrest, his trial and his sentencing to death. Max defends him and argues that society shares the blame for his crimes.

The section is about judgment and consequence, not Bigger's childhood or the Daltons' business.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: Bigger's life is shaped mainly by
section: This question is based on Native Son.
solution:
Bigger grows up poor and black in a society that limits his opportunities. His sense of fear, anger and worthlessness comes from poverty and racial oppression.

He is not a happy student, his parents are not wealthy, and the Daltons employ him rather than befriend him.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The repeated phrase “gently, gently” in Diop's poem suggests
section: This question is based on Vanity.
solution:
The persona says that even if the people speak “gently, gently” about their sufferings, no one will listen. The repetition creates a slow, hushed tone of restrained grief and regret.

It is not playful, violent or proud. The softness of the phrase makes the sorrow more painful.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The allusion to “blue Peter on empty ships” refers to

option.b: a blue ship on the sea
option.d: Peter's fruitless fishing in the Bible

section: This question is based on Ambush.
solution:
The line alludes to the biblical story of Peter, who fished all night and caught nothing until Jesus helped him. It stands for the people's hard work without reward.

“Blue” suggests sadness, and “petered out desires” means hopes that have faded away.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The “wailing piano” in Okara's poem represents
section: This question is based on Piano and Drums.
solution:
The piano speaks of “complex ways” and a “tear-furrowed concerto”. It stands for Western civilisation and modern life, which the persona finds complicated and troubling.

The drums, by contrast, represent the simple, primal African past.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The mood of Hallowell's poem is best described as
section: This question is based on The Dining Table.
solution:
The poem is filled with images of gun wounds, blood, dying vegetables, cholera and child soldiers. Its mood is therefore sorrowful and lamenting.

There is no cheerfulness, romance or peace in the description of the war-time “dinner”.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The statement “Hope is not a grain of sand” implies that hope is
section: This question is based on The Panic of Growing Older.
solution:
A grain of sand is tiny and easy to ignore. By saying that hope is not a grain of sand, the persona means that hope is not a small or worthless thing.

Hope still has weight and value, even though life brings disappointment.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The persona wishes to

option.d: blend the best of African and Western cultures

section: This question is based on The Anvil and the Hammer.
solution:
The persona stands between the anvil and the hammer, in the “forging house of a new life”. He wants to shape a new culture that keeps African roots while accepting what is useful from the West.

He does not want to reject all Western ideas, return to farming or abandon Africa.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The tone of Tennyson's poem is one of
section: This question is based on Crossing the Bar.
solution:
The persona speaks calmly about the “one clear call” and hopes that there will be “no moaning of the bar” when he sets out to sea. He accepts death with calm faith.

There is no panic, anger or mockery in the poem.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: God withholds rest from man so that man will
section: This question is based on The Pulley.
solution:
God says that if goodness does not lead man to Him, then weariness will “toss him to my breast”. The lack of rest makes man restless and draws him back to God.

The withholding of rest is therefore an act of love, not punishment.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The poem contrasts the school with
section: This question is based on The School Boy.
solution:
The boy longs for the summer morning, the birds and the open air, but school keeps him indoors “in sighing and dismay”. The poem sets nature against the confinement of school.

The main contrast is not between school and the city, home or church.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: “The Proud King” is best described as
section: This question is based on The Proud King.
solution:
The poem tells a story: King Jovinian boasts, is humiliated, loses his identity and later learns humility. Because it tells a story, it is a narrative poem.

A lyric expresses personal feeling, a sonnet has fourteen lines, and an ode is a poem of praise.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The character who works against the hero of a play or a novel is called the
solution:
The antagonist is the character who opposes the protagonist, creating the main conflict of the story.

The protagonist is the hero or main character. An anti-hero is a main character who lacks heroic qualities, and a clown is a comic figure.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: “He fights like a tiger whenever he is provoked” is an example of
solution:
The word like shows a direct comparison between the man's fighting and a tiger's ferocity. This is a simile.

A metaphor would say “he is a tiger”. Assonance repeats vowel sounds, hyperbole is exaggeration, and personification gives human qualities to non-human things.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: An epistolary novel is one written in the form of
solution:
An epistolary novel tells its story through a series of letters, diaries or similar documents.

It is not written as an essay, a play or mainly as a dialogue, although letters may contain dialogue.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: A simple story with a deeper meaning is called an
solution:
An allegory is a story whose characters and events stand for deeper moral, political or spiritual ideas.

An elegy mourns the dead, an ode is a poem of praise, and an epic is a long narrative poem about a hero.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The repetition of sentences or phrases using the same grammatical structure is known as
solution:
Parallelism is the repetition of a grammatical pattern in successive phrases or sentences, as in “I came, I saw, I conquered”.

It creates balance and rhythm. Merely repeating the same word is not necessarily parallelism.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The repetition of the same consonant sound at the beginning of words in a phrase is known as
solution:
Alliteration is the repetition of the same initial consonant sound in nearby words, such as “sweet silver song”.

Assonance repeats vowel sounds, consonance repeats consonant sounds within or at the end of words, and irony is a contrast between expectation and reality.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: A serious work of art that ends on a sad note is called a
solution:
A tragedy is a serious work that ends unhappily, usually with the suffering or death of the main character.

A comedy ends happily, a tragicomedy mixes sad and comic elements, and a melodrama uses exaggerated emotion and sensational events.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: A brief reference to a person, event or place in a work of art is called
solution:
An allusion is an indirect reference to a well-known person, event, place or literary work, such as a reference to the Bible or to Greek mythology.

Ambiguity means having more than one possible meaning, and atmosphere is the feeling of a place or scene.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: Robinson Crusoe in Daniel Defoe's novel of the same name is an example of a/an
solution:
An eponymous character is the character whose name forms the title of the work. Robinson Crusoe gives his name to the novel Robinson Crusoe.

The term has nothing to do with being sad, weak or minor.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: A recurring idea, image or group of images that unifies a literary work is called a
solution:
A motif is a recurring idea, image, phrase or symbol that helps to unify a literary work and develop its theme.

A legend is a traditional story, an anecdote is a short account of an incident, and a prelude is an introductory piece.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The lines about the drums and the dancers suggest that

option.a: music is more important than memory
option.b: the dancers have forgotten their culture
option.c: cultural memory survives even when its music fades
option.d: drums should never be played again

section:
“The drums have gone silent;
The dancers' feet remember
What the ears have forgotten.”
solution:
Even though the drums are silent, the dancers' feet still remember what the ears have forgotten. This means that cultural memory survives in the body and in practice, even when the music fades.

The lines do not dismiss memory, claim total forgetfulness or forbid drumming.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The figure of speech used in the description of her laughter is
section: Her laughter was a bell ringing across the field.
solution:
Her laughter is directly described as a bell, without using like or as. This is a metaphor.

A simile would use like or as. Onomatopoeia uses sound-imitating words, and an oxymoron joins opposite terms.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The figure of speech used in the description of the train is
section: The train sighed, shuddered, and then dragged its long body out of the station.
solution:
The train is said to sigh, shudder and drag its body, which are human actions. This is personification.

There is no substitution of an associated name, no deliberate exaggeration and no understatement.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The mood of the exchange between Ama and Kofi is one of
section:
AMA: You have come back.
KOFI: Only to collect what belongs to me.
AMA: Then take your shadow and go.
solution:
Kofi's cold purpose and Ama's bitter reply create an atmosphere of hostility and tension. She does not welcome him; she tells him to take his shadow and leave.

There is no joy, calmness or romance in the exchange.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The theme of the lines about the forest and the road is
section:
“They sold the forest to buy a road,
Then complained that the rain had lost its way.”
solution:
The people destroy the forest to build a road and then wonder why the rain no longer comes as it used to. The lines show the cost of reckless development and the loss of nature.

The poem is not praising forests, celebrating travel or teaching about rain in a simple way.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The figure of speech used in the description of the old man's face is
section: The old man's face was a map of roads he had never travelled.
solution:
The face is directly called a map covered with lines like roads. This is a metaphor.

A simile would say the face was like a map. A euphemism softens a harsh expression, and an apostrophe addresses an absent person or thing.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: “The pen is mightier than the sword” is an example of
solution:
The pen stands for writing, ideas and the press, while the sword stands for war and physical force. Using something associated with an idea to represent that idea is metonymy.

There is no comparison using like or as, no sound imitation and no seeming contradiction.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The device illustrated in the governor's declaration is
section: “Nobody is above the law,” the governor declared, as his convoy sped past the red light.
solution:
The governor says that nobody is above the law, yet his convoy breaks the law by speeding past a red light. The contrast between his words and his action is irony.

The passage does not exaggerate, repeat sounds or give human qualities to non-human things.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: Baroka opposes the railway because he

option.a: wants to protect the village market
option.b: has no land for the tracks
option.c: fears that progress will weaken his authority

section: This question is based on The Lion and the Jewel.
solution:
Baroka bribes the surveyor to divert the railway line away from Ilujinle. He fears that modern progress will reduce his power and importance in the village.

He pretends to be protecting tradition, but his real concern is his own position.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: Sidi finally agrees to marry Baroka after

option.d: she goes to mock him for his supposed impotence

section: This question is based on The Lion and the Jewel.
solution:
Sadiku tells Sidi that Baroka is impotent, and Sidi goes to his house to mock him. Baroka then proves his virility, wins her admiration and marries her.

Lakunle refuses to pay the bride price, so option A is wrong.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: Jimmy's bitterness is chiefly caused by

option.a: his unhappy past and social frustration

section: This question is based on Look Back in Anger.
solution:
Jimmy is a working-class graduate who feels trapped in a society that offers him little. He is angry about his painful past and his social and economic frustration.

He is educated and has friends like Cliff, so the other options do not explain his bitterness.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: In the middle of the play, Alison leaves Jimmy with
section: This question is based on Look Back in Anger.
solution:
After losing her baby, Alison leaves with her father, Colonel Redfern. She later returns at the end of the play.

Cliff and Helena are other characters in the house, and Hugh is Jimmy's friend from the past.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: Adah's greatest ambition as a child is to
section: This question is based on Second Class Citizen.
solution:
Adah wants to go to school and obtain an education, even though her society values boys more than girls. Education is her path to independence.

She does not dream first of nursing, a rich husband or America. Her academic ambition comes before everything else.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: Francis's attitude to Adah in England is best described as
section: This question is based on Second Class Citizen.
solution:
Francis expects Adah to work and support the family while he studies, yet he treats her with contempt and tries to control her. His attitude is exploitative and domineering.

He is not supportive, fair or humble towards her.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The novel has a

option.a: dual setting in Ghana and Nigeria

section: This question is based on Unexpected Joy at Dawn.
solution:
The novel moves between Ghana and Nigeria, following characters who cross borders in search of safety and a better life.

This dual setting allows the writer to compare the two countries and to expose the hardships of refugees.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: Nii's journey from Togo towards Nigeria is best described as
section: This question is based on Unexpected Joy at Dawn.
solution:
Nii travels in fear, without proper papers, through dangerous border routes. His journey is strenuous and risky.

The novel shows the humiliation, bribery and uncertainty that refugees face at borders.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The story is narrated mainly through
section: This question is based on Wuthering Heights.
solution:
Lockwood, a tenant at Thrushcross Grange, and Nelly Dean, the housekeeper, tell most of the story. Their accounts are passed on to the reader.

Heathcliff, Catherine and the others are characters in the story, not the main narrators.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: Heathcliff's love for Catherine is presented as
section: This question is based on Wuthering Heights.
solution:
Heathcliff's love for Catherine is fierce, possessive and lasting beyond death. It brings suffering to both families and is obsessive and destructive.

It is not gentle, casual or merely friendly.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: A dominant theme of Senghor's poem is

option.a: negritude and the celebration of African womanhood

section: This question is based on Black Woman.
solution:
Senghor praises the black woman as the source of life, beauty and African identity. The poem is a celebration of negritude and African womanhood.

It does not condemn African women or praise European cities, and old age is not its subject.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The poem is best described as
section: This question is based on The Leader and the Led.
solution:
The poem uses animals such as the lion, the antelope and the hyena to discuss how leaders are chosen. It is a fable about leadership, told through animal characters.

It is not a love poem, an elegy or a war song.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: Neto's poem focuses mainly on

option.c: the suffering of Africa under slavery and colonial rule
option.d: the beauty of the African savannah

section: This question is based on The Grieved Lands.
solution:
The Grieved Lands mourns the pain of Africa caused by slavery, exploitation and colonial rule. Its central concern is the suffering of the continent and its people.

The poem does not celebrate city wealth, pure joy or scenic beauty.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The poem celebrates the women's
section: This question is based on The Song of the Women of My Land.
solution:
Sesay presents women who work in the fields, suffer oppression and yet keep their dignity and song alive. The poem celebrates their endurance and quiet strength.

The women are poor and oppressed, not wealthy, powerful or fond of travel.

Therefore, option D is correct.
category: The Song of the Women of My Land

question: “What can be worthy of your life?” is an example of
section: This question is based on Raider of the Treasure Trove.
solution:
The line asks a question that is not meant to be answered directly. It makes the reader think about the purpose of life, so it is a rhetorical question.

An apostrophe addresses someone absent or a thing, personification gives human qualities to non-human things, and mime is silent action.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: “And it sent him home / Home to rest in peace” is an example of
section: This question is based on A Government Driver on His Retirement.
solution:
“Rest in peace” is a gentle way of saying that the driver died. Using a mild expression instead of the harsh word death is euphemism.

Irony is a contrast between expectation and reality, an oxymoron joins opposite words, and hyperbole is exaggeration.

Therefore, option B is correct.
category: A Government Driver on His Retirement

question: “And make one little room an everywhere” is an example of
section: This question is based on The Good Morrow.
solution:
The lover says that one small room can become the whole world. This is a deliberate exaggeration (hyperbole) that expresses the greatness of love.

It is not a mild expression, a mere image or a reference to another text.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The central concern of Angelou's poem is

option.d: the longing for freedom under oppression

section: This question is based on Caged Bird.
solution:
The free bird enjoys the sky while the caged bird can only sing of freedom it does not have. The poem's central concern is the longing for freedom under oppression.

The birds are symbols, not the subject of a simple nature poem about singing or farming.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The journey in Eliot's poem is a metaphor for

option.a: a spiritual journey of faith and change

section: This question is based on The Journey of the Magi.
solution:
The Magi's difficult journey to Bethlehem is used to represent a spiritual journey that leads to faith, doubt and a painful change of life.

It is not a holiday, a business trip or a military campaign.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The poem is addressed to
section: This question is based on Do Not Go Gentle into That Good Night.
solution:
Dylan Thomas wrote the poem for his dying father. He urges him to “rage, rage against the dying of the light” rather than accept death quietly.

The poem is personal, not addressed to a son, a soldier or the general reader.

Therefore, option B is correct.
category: Do Not Go Gentle into That Good Night

question: Hopkins's poem mourns

option.c: the felling of the poplar trees

section: This question is based on Binsey Poplars.
solution:
The poem is an elegy for the poplar trees at Binsey that were cut down. Hopkins laments the destruction of nature and the beauty that can never be restored.

It is not about a friend's death, a flood or a war.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: “Black piper on an infinitesimal pipe” is an example of
section: This question is based on Bat.
solution:
The bat is directly called a black piper with a tiny pipe. This is a metaphor that compares the bat's cry to the music of a piper.

There is no comic imitation, no repetition and no direct giving of human form to the bat, although the image is imaginative.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The basic outline of a story arranged in a logical and sequential order is known as the
solution:
The plot is the arrangement of events in a story in a logical and sequential order, with a beginning, middle and end.

A storyline is a looser word for the main story, narration is the act of telling, and setting is the time and place of the action.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The pattern of rhymes at the ends of lines in a poem is called the
solution:
A rhyme scheme is the pattern of end rhymes in a poem, usually shown with letters such as ABAB or AABB.

Rhythm is the beat of the poem, metre is the measured arrangement of stressed and unstressed syllables, and a stanza is a group of lines.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: “When the sun began to yawn” is an instance of
solution:
The sun is given the human action of yawning. This is personification, which gives human qualities to non-human things.

Hyperbole is exaggeration, and comedy is a genre, not a figure of speech. “Impersonation” is not the literary term for this device.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: Flashback is a technique by which

option.b: a scene is repeated for emphasis
option.d: a past event is recalled to shed light on the present

solution:
A flashback interrupts the present action to show an earlier event. It helps the audience understand the characters and the present situation.

It is not about physical movement, simple repetition or an abrupt ending.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The study, analysis, interpretation and evaluation of literary works is called
solution:
Criticism is the study, analysis, interpretation and evaluation of literary works. A critic explains what a work means and judges how well it achieves its purpose.

A summary shortens a text, appreciation is enjoyment and understanding of literature, and a biography is the life story of a person.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: Action, time and place in drama are regarded as the
solution:
The three unities of drama are the unity of action, the unity of time and the unity of place. They require a play to follow one main action within a short period and in one setting.

The other options are not the accepted literary term.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: A poem that does not conform to the regular rules of metre, rhyme or line length is called
solution:
Free verse is poetry without a fixed metre or rhyme scheme. It relies on rhythm, imagery and line arrangement rather than regular patterns.

Blank verse is different: it has no rhyme but keeps a regular metre, usually iambic pentameter.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: A poem written to mourn the dead is called an
solution:
An elegy is a poem of mourning for someone who has died. It expresses sorrow and often praises the dead person.

A dirge is a funeral song, a eulogy is a speech of praise for the dead, and an ode is a poem of praise for a person or thing, usually living.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: Romantic poetry is chiefly concerned with

option.a: the beauty of nature and strong feeling
option.b: love between a man and a woman only

solution:
Romantic poetry values nature, imagination, emotion and individual experience. It often celebrates the beauty of the natural world and deep personal feeling.

Although love poems exist, romance as a literary movement is wider than love between a man and a woman. It has nothing to do with Roman poets or science.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: A character whose qualities contrast with those of the protagonist is called a
solution:
A foil is a character whose qualities contrast with another character's, usually the protagonist. The contrast helps to highlight the protagonist's traits.

A villain is an evil character, a narrator tells the story, and a chorus comments on the action.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The lines above suggest that dispossession
section:
“I have no hate for the man
Who took my land;
I only pity the children
Who will inherit his hunger.”
solution:
The speaker does not hate the man who took the land; he pities the children who will inherit the hunger that comes with it. This shows that dispossession harms future generations.

The lines do not say that the harm ends, that people become rich or that the wrong is easily forgotten.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: “The road was a ribbon of moonlight” is an example of
solution:
The road is directly called a ribbon of moonlight, with no like or as. This is a metaphor.

A simile would use like or as. Metonymy substitutes an associated name, and apostrophe addresses an absent person or thing.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The mood created by the sentence above is one of
section: The village slept, and even the dogs refused to bark.
solution:
When even the dogs refuse to bark, the silence is more than ordinary quiet. The sentence creates a mood of unnatural stillness, as if something is about to happen.

There is no festive excitement, romance or protest in the description.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: Ngozi's reply in the extract above shows that she

option.b: refuses to endorse what she does not believe

section:
PAT: Sign here.
NGOZI: My hand will not betray my mouth.
solution:
Ngozi means that she will not sign a document that contradicts what she has said or believes. Her reply shows that she refuses to endorse something she does not agree with.

She is not illiterate, afraid or confused; she is making a firm moral choice.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The theme of the lines about the sea and the fathers is
section:
“The sea has swallowed our fathers
And given us salt for inheritance.”
solution:
The sea has taken the fathers and left the children only salt, a symbol of tears and hardship. The lines are about loss and inherited suffering.

They do not celebrate the wealth of the sea, the joy of fishing or the beauty of salt.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: “Her voice was soft as wool” is an example of
solution:
The word as makes a direct comparison between her voice and wool. This is a simile.

A metaphor would say her voice was wool. Personification gives human qualities to non-human things, and hyperbole is exaggeration.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: The device illustrated in the sentence above is
section: The teacher praised honesty all morning, then pocketed the examination fees.
solution:
The teacher praises honesty but then steals the examination fees. The contrast between the words and the action is irony.

There is no sound repetition, sound imitation or mild substitute for a harsh word.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: The figure of speech used in the description of fear is
section: Fear walked beside him all the way home.
solution:
Fear is described as walking beside him, which is a human action. This is personification.

There is no comparison using like or as, no substitution of an associated name and no balancing of opposites.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: Lakunle's refusal to pay the bride price is presented as

option.a: a sign of his poverty only

section: This question is based on The Lion and the Jewel.
solution:
Lakunle says that bride price treats women like goods and claims that he is modern. His refusal is presented as his embrace of modern ideas, although the villagers see it as stinginess.

He is not acting from religious duty or trying to marry Sadiku.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: Sadiku's role in the play is mainly that of
section: This question is based on The Lion and the Jewel.
solution:
Sadiku is Baroka's senior wife. She collects brides for him and carries news between him and Sidi.

She is not Sidi's mother, the village teacher or the stranger's guide.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: Cliff's role in the play is mainly that of
section: This question is based on Look Back in Anger.
solution:
Cliff lives with Jimmy and Alison and tries to keep peace between them. He is gentle, loyal and concerned for both of them, so he acts as a peacemaker and loyal friend.

He is not a trouble-maker, Alison's father or Jimmy's employer.

Therefore, option A is correct.

question: Helena leaves Jimmy at the end because she

option.b: cannot face Alison after her return

section: This question is based on Look Back in Anger.
solution:
When Alison returns, Helena realises that she has taken her friend's husband. Her conscience troubles her, and she cannot face Alison, so she leaves.

She is not leaving for a job, because her love has ended or because she fears Cliff.

Therefore, option B is correct.

question: The novel criticises a society that

option.c: values male children above female children

section: This question is based on Second Class Citizen.
solution:
Adah's family and community treat boys as more important than girls. She has to struggle for the education that her brother is given more easily. The novel criticises a society that values male children above female children.

It does not praise unequal pay for women, forbid marriage or encourage girls to study medicine.

Therefore, option C is correct.

question: The title refers to the inferior status given to

option.d: black people and women in a white male society

section: This question is based on Second Class Citizen.
solution:
The title points to the way black immigrants and women are treated as less important in British society. Adah is treated as a “second-class citizen” because of her race and sex.

The title is not about wealthy Nigerians, schoolchildren or civil servants in general.

Therefore, option D is correct.

question: A central theme of the novel is

option.a: the suffering of refugees and migrants

section: This question is based on Unexpected Joy at Dawn.
solution:
The novel follows characters who are forced to flee their homes and cross borders in search of safety. Its central theme is the suffering of refugees and migrants.

It does not celebrate military rule, European cities or smuggling.

Therefore, option A is correct.
